decisions: THE DEFERRED ENTRY'S COUNT WAS WRONG, AND THE EXTRA ONE MUST NOT BE CONSOLIDATED. Section 7 said 'StationPricing is hand-rolled in three places'. FOUR files declared a shape carrying the two price columns; the missed one was WaterStationInput in app/trips/actions.ts, and it is the WRITE shape. It deliberately omits `key` - the immutable FK target for trips.water_station, generated once on create and NEVER present in an update payload - plus `id` and `active`. Merging it would have put all three back within reach of the edit form, so following the deferred note literally would have introduced a real defect.

THE THREE THAT WERE DUPLICATED WERE BYTE-IDENTICAL - ten fields, same order, matching the 'every station' select: app/trips/page.tsx (declared FUNCTION-LOCALLY, invisible to the two client components mirroring it), ProjectsBoard.tsx and WaterStationsModal.tsx. All three now import WaterStationRow from lib/station-pricing, expressed as `StationOption & {...}` so a full row IS a pickable option plus admin fields and anything taking a StationOption accepts a row without a cast.

WHY IT WAS WORTH DOING EVEN THOUGH ALL THREE COPIES AGREED: the shape carries two PRICE columns and this schema's central rule is that NULL and 0 mean different things (not offered vs offered free). Three hand-written copies is exactly how a `?? 0` fix lands in one file and not the others. The two price columns now have EXACTLY ONE declaration in the repo (lib/station-pricing.ts:22).

STALE COMMENTS FROM 0122 SWEPT IN THE SAME PASS. Three comments still described the flat fill_cost as present hours after it was dropped: WaterStationInput's own doc ('stays on the table until its own retirement migration'), WaterStationsModal's header, and OperationStationsModal's 'no key, no fill_cost' contrast - which compared against a column that no longer exists.

RE-MEASURE A DEFERRED ITEM'S PREMISE BEFORE EXECUTING ON IT. Applied three times now, wrong three different ways: 0121's premise was FALSE (a concept-merge with zero rows to merge), 0122's was RIGHT but implied an already-closed sub-item, and this one's COUNT was low AND one of the uncounted sites was a trap.
